This guide covers 24 live music spots in Chattanooga: local bars, free outdoor concert series, larger venues, and annual festivals. Most are in or near downtown. The outdoor concert series run only in warmer months.
Chattanooga has deep music roots. Bessie Smith, known as the Empress of the Blues, grew up here and busked on its streets before becoming the most popular blues singer of the 1930s. The Glenn Miller Orchestra popularized “Chattanooga Choo Choo” in 1941 — it became the first recording to earn a Gold Record, selling 1.2 million copies.
The Category filter separates the guide into its four sections. Use Recurring Events to find the free outdoor concert series. Use Festivals to narrow to multi-day annual events. The Bluegrass filter shows four spots with a roots and folk focus.
The Free filter returns seven options with no admission cost. These include Nightfall, Riverfront Nights, the 3 Sisters Festival, and the Chattanooga Jazz Fest. All four outdoor series are also all-ages.
If there is a live music spot worth adding, send an email. Details change. Confirm before you go.

Live Music Bars in Chattanooga.

Bars and smaller venues run shows on most nights of the week in Chattanooga. The Woodshop in St. Elmo and JJ’s Bohemia are dedicated music bars. Sluggo’s downstairs lounge covers the underground and punk side. Charles & Myrtle’s is the only alcohol-free option with no cover. Several Southside breweries also host weekend music.

Breweries with live music

Free Outdoor Concert Series.

Four recurring outdoor concert series run from spring through fall. Nightfall (Fridays) and Riverfront Nights (Saturdays) both anchor downtown. Cambridge Square runs Saturday nights in Ooltewah, about 20 minutes east. The River Market adds music to its Saturday vendor market most weeks. All four series are free and open to all ages.

Chattanooga outdoor adventures

Larger Music Venues in Chattanooga.

The Tivoli Foundation covers the high-production end, with three historic venues for national acts. The Signal and Barrelhouse Ballroom fill the mid-sized tier with more variety. Songbirds and Barking Legs Theater are smaller but book more adventurous lineups. For theater, symphony, and dance, see the performing arts guide.

Chattanooga performing arts guide

Music Festivals in Chattanooga.

Chattanooga hosts several annual music festivals. IBMA World of Bluegrass is now based here through at least 2027. The 3 Sisters Festival and Chattanooga Jazz Fest are both free, held in the fall at downtown venues. Smart Music Fest debuted in 2025 at Ross’s Landing. Riverbend and Moon River are both on hiatus or relocated.

1. The Woodshop Listening Room .

A neighborhood bar on St. Elmo Ave, in a historic district house. The room is small and built around live music. The music leans toward bluegrass and folk. It draws both locals and visitors throughout the year. Check social media for the current show schedule.

2. JJ's Bohemia .

A dive bar that has hosted live music since 2006. The staff are welcoming and the atmosphere is casual. Many genres appear on the calendar throughout the week. Check their Facebook page for upcoming shows.

3. Buds Sports Bar .

A sports bar in East Ridge, just outside Chattanooga. Live bands play on Friday and Saturday nights. Expect loud rock from acts like Aunt Betty or Local Slim. Check their calendar for show dates.

4. Sluggo's North Vegetarian Cafe .

A vegan diner and full bar on Cherokee Blvd in Northshore. The downstairs lounge hosts punk, indie, and underground shows. The lounge runs Wednesday through Saturday nights and is 21 and over. Grab food upstairs before the show.

5. Charles & Myrtle's Coffeehouse .

A small, all-ages listening room on McBrien Road, inside Christ Unity Church. Every show is acoustic. The lineup covers folk, blues, bluegrass, and jazz. No alcohol is served. Call (423) 892-4960 for the next show date.

11. TVFCU Riverfront Nights .

A free Saturday concert series at Ross's Landing from Memorial Day to Labor Day. Local artists perform from 7PM. Food and drink vendors open at 6PM. The show runs rain or shine. Bring a chair.

12. Nightfall .

Chattanooga's original free concert series, now in its 39th year. National and international acts play every Friday night from May through July at Miller Plaza and Miller Park. Food trucks and vendors open at 6PM. Music starts at 7PM. Bring a chair.

13. Cambridge Square .

A Saturday night outdoor concert series at Cambridge Square in Ooltewah from April to October. The music rotates through rock, country, jazz, and bluegrass. Events are weather permitting. Check the website before heading out.

14. Chattanooga River Market .

A Saturday market in spring, summer, and fall with artisan goods and produce. Live music from local artists is a regular part of the event. Good for a relaxed weekend morning. Check the website for dates.

15. Tivoli Theatre Foundation .

A nonprofit that runs three historic downtown venues: Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Auditorium, the Tivoli Theatre, and the Walker Theatre. The Tivoli reopened in October 2026 after a $75 million restoration. The 1921 room now seats just over 1,600 and allows in-seat drink service. Check their calendar for shows across all three venues.

16. The Signal .

A concert hall on the historic Chattanooga Choo Choo grounds. National touring acts perform here regularly. Ages 14 and under must be accompanied by an adult. Check the calendar for upcoming shows.

17. Barrelhouse Ballroom .

A mid-sized venue designed to fill a gap in Chattanooga's live music options. Food, drink, and music at reasonable prices. The lineup covers many genres throughout the year. Check their calendar for upcoming shows.

18. Songbirds .

A nonprofit music venue at 206 W Main Street with two bars and a patio. Songbirds moved here from the Choo Choo in 2024. Ticket sales support music education for local youth. The calendar covers both touring and local acts.

19. Barking Legs Theater .

An intimate arts venue on Dodds Ave, in operation since 1993, with seating for about 150. Wednesday jazz nights and a Monday Nite Big Band run regularly. The booking also covers Irish traditional, big band, and experimental acts. No other Chattanooga venue books the same mix.

20. IBMA World of Bluegrass .

The International Bluegrass Music Association's annual convention, now based in Chattanooga through at least 2027. The 2026 edition ran October 20-24 at the Chattanooga Convention Center. Events include the Bluegrass Ramble showcases across downtown, the Bluegrass Music Awards, and a two-day outdoor festival. It draws tens of thousands to town.

21. Smart Music Fest .

A multi-stage music festival that debuted at Ross's Landing in May 2025. The lineup covers pop-eclectic and electronic music across four stages. The event includes an art garden, about 30 food trucks, and a craft beer tent. Dates for the next edition are TBA. Check the website for updates.

22. 3 Sisters Festival .

A free two-day bluegrass festival at Ross's Landing in the fall, with the stage set over the Tennessee River. It has run as a Chattanooga tradition since 2007. Local vendors set up on-site. The 2026 lineup featured Sam Bush, The Travelin' McCourys, and Rhonda Vincent.

23. Chattanooga Jazz Fest .

A free one-day festival at the Choo Choo Gardens featuring local jazz, blues, and funk players. The 2026 event featured 10 or more acts and an all-day market. The day ends with an open jam at Wanderlinger Brewing. Check the website for next year's date.

24. Riverbend & Moon River Festivals .

Two Chattanooga music festivals that no longer run downtown. Riverbend remains on hiatus; its organizer now points to the free Riverfront Nights series instead. Moon River returned in 2026 as 'Moon River At Sea,' a November cruise from Miami. Check their websites for any future Chattanooga dates.

Bars with regular live music are scattered across Chattanooga’s neighborhoods. St. Elmo, Northshore, and downtown each have their own spots. Combining two or three in one evening is easy when they’re close together.
For outdoor concert series, check schedules before heading out. Nightfall runs Friday nights. Riverfront Nights runs Saturday nights. Cambridge Square in Ooltewah is about 20 minutes east. Bring a chair for any outdoor show.
Several breweries also host live music on weekends. The Chattanooga breweries guide covers Wanderlinger, Oddstory, and others with taproom music.

FAQ.

Where can I find live music in Chattanooga on a weeknight?

Several bars host live music on weeknights. JJ’s Bohemia runs shows throughout the week. Tremont Tavern has a Tuesday open mic. Barking Legs Theater hosts Wednesday jazz nights and a Monday Nite Big Band. Check individual venue calendars before you go, as schedules rotate.

Are there free live music concerts in Chattanooga?

Yes. Nightfall (Fridays, May-July), TVFCU Riverfront Nights (Saturdays, Memorial Day to Labor Day), and Cambridge Square (Saturdays, April-October) are all free outdoor series. The 3 Sisters bluegrass festival and Chattanooga Jazz Fest are also free. Charles & Myrtle’s Coffeehouse has no cover.

What is the IBMA World of Bluegrass, and when does it come to Chattanooga?

The International Bluegrass Music Association’s annual convention moved from Raleigh, NC to Chattanooga. The 2026 event ran October 20-24. It includes the Bluegrass Music Awards, the Bluegrass Ramble showcases across downtown venues, and a two-day outdoor festival. It is scheduled to continue in Chattanooga through at least 2027.

What are good all-ages live music venues in Chattanooga?

The free outdoor series - Nightfall, Riverfront Nights, Cambridge Square, and the River Market - are all all-ages. Charles & Myrtle’s is an all-ages, alcohol-free acoustic listening room. Tivoli Theatre Foundation venues, Songbirds, Barrelhouse Ballroom, and Barking Legs Theater all welcome all ages.

What happened to Riverbend Festival in Chattanooga?

Riverbend Festival remains on hiatus. The nonprofit that ran it, Friends of the Festival, now points to the free Riverfront Nights series as its main summer offering. Riverbend was Chattanooga’s original multi-day music festival. No announced return date as of 2026.

Where can I see bluegrass music in Chattanooga?

The Woodshop in St. Elmo leans toward bluegrass and folk most nights. Cambridge Square in Ooltewah books bluegrass on its Saturday outdoor stage. The 3 Sisters Festival at Ross’s Landing is a free fall bluegrass event. IBMA World of Bluegrass, now based in Chattanooga, is the largest bluegrass gathering in the country.
